_comment: Study #3 -- Humility in Metaphysics. Comprehensive Intellectual Humility Scale (Krumrei-Mancuso & Rouse, 2016), 22 items, 4 subscales. English item text is the canonical/stored text (same convention as every other instrument in this catalog -- see SPSS_to_Firebird_Mapping.md Section 2); the Portuguese (Brazil) draft translation respondents will actually see lives in 12.gdx.virtology/Intellectual_Humility_Scale_PT_Adaptation.md, not in this intake. No cardiac-coherence component. Per GDX_H7ph_Plan_Study_Humility_in_Metaphysics.md Phase 1.

study.title: Humility in Metaphysics
study.objective: Pilot-test a Portuguese (Brazil) draft adaptation of the Comprehensive Intellectual Humility Scale (Krumrei-Mancuso & Rouse, 2016) and explore its correspondence with the Septenary Constitution, Kundalini Chakras, Thomas Aquinas's Five Ways, and the Virtology virtue of Humility.
study.method: Cross-sectional self-report questionnaire, single wave. 22-item, 4-subscale Likert instrument; no cardiac-coherence component.

instruments.name: Comprehensive Intellectual Humility Scale
instruments.description: Krumrei-Mancuso, E. J., & Rouse, S. V. (2016). The development and validation of the Comprehensive Intellectual Humility Scale. Journal of Personality Assessment, 98, 209-221. Portuguese (Brazil) draft adaptation, forward-translation only (not yet back-translated, committee-reviewed, or psychometrically re-validated) -- see 12.gdx.virtology/Intellectual_Humility_Scale_PT_Adaptation.md.
instruments.instructions: Carefully read each statement and indicate the degree to which you agree each statement is true for you.
instruments.phenomenon_description: Disposition to recognize the limits of one's own knowledge, remain non-defensive when one's beliefs are challenged, and give fair consideration to viewpoints different from one's own.

constructs.name: Intellectual Humility
constructs.definition: Disposition to recognize the limits of one's own knowledge, remain non-defensive when one's beliefs are challenged, and give fair consideration to viewpoints different from one's own.

variables.name: Independence of Intellect and Ego (Intellectual Humility)
variables.description: Degree to which the person's sense of self-worth is independent of whether others agree with their important beliefs.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of 5 reverse-scored Likert items (16,17,18,21,22), 1-5 scale each.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 5 reverse-scored items feeding this dimension.

variables.name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)
variables.description: Willingness to change an important belief or opinion in light of good reasons or new information.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of 5 Likert items (6-10), 1-5 scale each.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 5 items feeding this dimension.

variables.name: Respect for Others' Viewpoints (Intellectual Humility)
variables.description: Capacity to respect and acknowledge the merit of a viewpoint one disagrees with.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of 6 Likert items (11,13,14,15,19,20), 1-5 scale each.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 6 items feeding this dimension.

variables.name: Lack of Intellectual Overconfidence (Intellectual Humility)
variables.description: Degree to which the person does not overestimate the certainty or superiority of their own beliefs.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of 6 reverse-scored Likert items (1,2,3,4,5,12), 1-5 scale each.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 6 reverse-scored items feeding this dimension.

items.statement_text: My ideas are usually better than other people's ideas.
For the most part, others have more to learn from me than I have to learn from them.
When I am really confident in a belief, there is very little chance that belief is wrong.
I'd rather rely on my own knowledge about most topics than turn to others for expertise.
On important topics, I am not likely to be swayed by the viewpoints of others.
I have at times changed opinions that were important to me, when someone showed me I was wrong.
items.variable_name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I am willing to change my position on an important issue in the face of good reasons.
items.variable_name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I am open to revising my important beliefs in the face of new information.
items.variable_name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I am willing to change my opinions on the basis of compelling reason.
items.variable_name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I'm willing to change my mind once it's made up about an important topic.
items.variable_name: Openness to Revising One's Viewpoint (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I respect that there are ways of making important decisions that are different from the way I make decisions.
Listening to perspectives of others seldom changes my important opinions.
I welcome different ways of thinking about important topics.
I can have great respect for someone, even when we don't see eye-to-eye on important topics.
Even when I disagree with others, I can recognize that they have sound points.
When someone disagrees with ideas that are important to me, it feels as though I'm being attacked.
items.variable_name: Independence of Intellect and Ego (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: When someone contradicts my most important beliefs, it feels like a personal attack.
items.variable_name: Independence of Intellect and Ego (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I tend to feel threatened when others disagree with me on topics that are close to my heart.
items.variable_name: Independence of Intellect and Ego (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I can respect others, even if I disagree with them in important ways.
I am willing to hear others out, even if I disagree with them.
When someone disagrees with ideas that are important to me, it makes me feel insignificant.
items.variable_name: Independence of Intellect and Ego (Intellectual Humility)

items.statement_text: I feel small when others disagree with me on topics that are close to my heart.
